paragraph: The world's population has increased dramatically over the past century. In 1950, approximately 2.5 billion people lived on Earth, compared with 3.0 billion in 1960 and 6.1 billion in 2000. By 2024, the global population had reached approximately 8.2 billion. This growth reflects improvements in healthcare, sanitation, nutrition, and life expectancy.

Canada's population has grown considerably since the middle of the 20th century. In 1950, the country had approximately 14 million residents, increasing to around 18.2 million by 1960 and 30.7 million by 2000. By 2024, Canada's population had reached approximately 39.7 million. The United Nations projects that it could reach approximately 46.1 million by 2054.

India has experienced substantial population growth since independence in 1947. Its population was approximately 376 million in 1950, increased to around 1.05 billion by 2000, and reached approximately 1.45 billion in 2024. India is projected to have approximately 1.68 billion people by 2050. Population growth is expected to slow as fertility rates decline.

China's population experienced rapid growth throughout much of the 20th century. It had approximately 544 million residents in 1950, compared with 1.26 billion in 2000 and approximately 1.42 billion in 2021. Its population subsequently began declining, reaching approximately 1.42 billion in 2024. United Nations projections suggest that China's population could fall to approximately 633 million by 2100.

The United Nations projects that the global population will continue growing over the coming decades, although the growth rate will gradually decrease. Its 2024 medium projection estimates approximately 9.8 billion people by 2054 and approximately 10.2 billion by 2100. The population is expected to peak at around 10.3 billion during the 2080s. These projections depend on future fertility, mortality, and migration patterns.

If you are planning a road trip from Toronto to Montreal, the driving distance is approximately 543 km, depending on your route. At an average speed of 100 km/h, the journey would take approximately 5.4 hours without stops. A vehicle consuming 8 L of fuel per 100 km would use approximately 43.4 L for the trip. You should also account for traffic, rest breaks, and possible construction delays.

A trip from Vancouver to Calgary covers approximately 970 km by road, depending on the chosen route. If you drive at an average speed of 90 km/h, the journey would require approximately 10.8 hours of driving. For a vehicle with a fuel consumption rate of 9 L per 100 km, the trip would require approximately 87.3 L of fuel. Mountain weather and road conditions can significantly affect travel times.

When preparing a basic pancake recipe for 4 people, you can use 250 g of all-purpose flour, 300 mL of milk, and 2 large eggs. Add approximately 30 g of melted butter and 15 g of sugar to improve the flavour and texture. Mix the ingredients until combined, then cook each pancake for approximately 2 minutes per side. This recipe should produce around 8 medium-sized pancakes.

For a simple pasta dinner serving 4 people, prepare approximately 400 g of dry pasta and 2 L of water for boiling. Add around 20 g of salt to the cooking water and prepare a sauce using 400 g of crushed tomatoes, 15 mL of olive oil, and 10 g of minced garlic. Most dried pasta takes approximately 8–12 minutes to cook, depending on its shape and thickness. Reserve approximately 120 mL of pasta water before draining if you want to adjust the sauce consistency.

A standard baking recipe for 12 muffins might require 250 g of flour, 150 g of sugar, 120 mL of milk, and 100 g of melted butter. You would also need approximately 2 large eggs, 10 g of baking powder, and 2 mL of vanilla extract. Bake the muffins at 180°C for approximately 18–22 minutes. Allow them to cool for at least 10 minutes before removing them from the baking tray.
